clue.text: Relatively superior man always looking in the yearbook

definitions.meaning: an older male sibling, superior in age within the family, hence relatively
the ever-watching leader in Orwell's novel named after a year, Nineteen Eighty-Four

explanation.walkthrough: 'The yearbook' is Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four, whose title is a year; its slogan says this figure is always watching.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an elder sibling in a family; the other is Orwell's all-seeing dictator figure.

clue.text: Plant having insect damage

parts.note: a bug is any small insect
loss is harm or damage suffered

explanation.surface: A garden plant has been ravaged by insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugloss is a bristly flowering herb of the borage family.

clue.text: Fails to enter into welcome, being most selfish

indicators.note: one word is asked to go inside the other, so the dying word sits within the greeting

parts.note: to greet is to welcome
an engine that dies fails

explanation.surface: Someone is denied a welcome because they are the most selfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed is selfish wanting, so the greediest person is the most grasping.

clue.text: Appear with relative frequency to arrest some Mafia?

parts.note: to run in a suspect is slang for arresting them
the Mafia is organised in clans, each called a family

explanation.surface: Police seem to keep arresting members of the Mafia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relative' is a pun: a trait that turns up often among relatives is hereditary.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait found across generations of relatives is hereditary, common among kin.

clue.text: Projection about top honours to be accepted

indicators.note: the projecting joint goes round the cards, so it is written about them

parts.note: a tenon is the projecting piece of a woodworking joint
in bridge the ace and king are the top honour cards, A and K

explanation.surface: A protruding feature with high awards is due to be approved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Projection' looks like a forecast, but it is the jutting carpentry joint that fits a mortise; in bridge the ace and king are the highest honour cards.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on staff or work is to accept them.

clue.text: In calm time, I had established patent

indicators.note: the contraction is set in the calm-plus-time word, signalled by placing it in that run

parts.note: even means calm or placid
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: During a quiet period someone set up a patent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patent' looks like a noun for an invention, but here it is the adjective meaning obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent as an adjective means plain or obvious to see.

clue.text: Desire to have evil woman beheaded

indicators.note: cutting off the head removes the first letter of the woman's word

parts.note: a witch is a woman thought to use evil magic

explanation.surface: Someone longs to see a wicked woman executed.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a restless craving or longing for something.

clue.text: Counterpart to East wind

parts.note: a twin is an exact counterpart
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: An easterly gale has a matching partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as a breeze, but it is the verb, to coil.
explanation.definitionFit: To twine is to twist or coil around something.

clue.text: Important letter read out in meal

parts.note: high means important, as in high office

indicators.note: a letter spoken aloud is heard as its name

parts.note: the letter T, whose spoken name is the drink

explanation.surface: A significant character is announced at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: High tea is a substantial early-evening meal in Britain, taken with tea.

clue.text: Bill thus demanded when Hoover was installed?

definitions.text: Bill thus demanded when Hoover was installed?

parts.words: Bill thus demanded when Hoover was installed?
parts.note: a casual request for the bill, reread as a question about the great barrier built on the Colorado River and named after a president

explanation.walkthrough: Hoover looks like the vacuum cleaner, but the Hoover Dam is meant; installing it puts a DAM in the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial way of asking how much one owes or must pay.

clue.text: Make thin pickings round a depressed area

indicators.note: the valley word goes round the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a glen is a narrow valley, a hollow in the land

explanation.surface: Someone scrapes a meagre living in a deprived district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depressed area' suggests economic hardship, but it is a literal dip in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather leftover scraps, small gleanings after harvest.

clue.text: Head of state puts in roughly half a day conferring honours

indicators.note: the monarch takes the dark hours into himself, so they go inside

parts.note: a king is a head of state
night is about half of the twenty-four hours

explanation.surface: A monarch spends half a day handing out awards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubbing someone a knight confers a title upon them.

clue.text: Would-be priest stopped short by church decree

indicators.note: cutting short removes the final letter of the trainee's word

parts.note: an ordinand is a candidate for ordination
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A trainee cleric is halted by a ruling of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an authoritative order or law.

clue.text: Taking things amiss

parts.note: reads as being offended, but means wrongfully helping oneself to property

explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking things amiss' usually means getting offended; here it is taking goods wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is taking another's belongings unlawfully.

clue.text: He spent foolishly as king

indicators.note: spending foolishly suggests the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A monarch squandered his money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foolishly' rearranges HESPENT. King Stephen ruled England 1135-1154.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen was a twelfth-century English monarch.

clue.text: Bottom line she accepted

parts.note: reads as agreeing a final figure, but Bottom is the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream whom the fairy queen falls for

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom line' sounds like accounts; Bottom is Shakespeare's weaver given an ass's head and loved by the fairy queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen of the Fairies in the play dotes on Bottom under a love spell.

clue.text: Holding scripture, men read badly in church

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold the scripture abbreviation inside them
reading badly mangles the letters into a new order

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Men read scripture poorly in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges the letters of 'men read', and 'Holding' wraps them round the scripture abbreviation. Notre-Dame is the great Paris cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Notre-Dame is a famous Paris cathedral, a church.

clue.text: Drug in large quantity is deplorable

indicators.note: the drug letter goes in the quantity word

parts.note: a hatful is a large amount
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: Taking drugs in large amounts is shameful.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hateful is detestable, worthy of disgust.

clue.text: Rumour of some corn amid the grass

indicators.note: the corn sits amid the grass letters, inside them

parts.note: hay is dried grass
ears are the grain-bearing heads of corn

explanation.surface: Gossip about corn growing in a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearsay is information heard from others, unverified talk.

clue.text: Sensible man serving in pub

indicators.note: the soldier goes in the pub word

parts.note: a local is one's neighbourhood pub
a GI is an American serviceman

explanation.surface: A level-headed man works in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man serving' suggests a barman, but it is a soldier serving in the forces. A British 'local' is one's regular pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Logical reasoning is rational and sound.

clue.text: Fold in body old people had near stomach

parts.note: men are people
tum is informal for stomach

explanation.surface: Elderly folk have a fold of flesh near their bellies.
explanation.definitionFit: The omentum is a fold of membrane in the abdomen.

clue.text: 20 could be unsavoury, according to Matthew

definitions.meaning: the answer to 20 is a sailor, which an old seadog is

definitions.text: could be unsavoury, according to Matthew
definitions.meaning: Matthew 5:13 warns that salt can lose its savour, so salt grown old might taste of nothing

explanation.walkthrough: Matthew's Gospel says 'if the salt have lost his savour'; aged salt would be unsavoury.
explanation.definitionFit: An experienced sailor is called an old sea-hand, a seadog.

clue.text: Sailor's'chance to support his officer

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower piece holds up the upper, so chance comes after officer

parts.note: a mate is a ship's officer
lot means chance, as in drawing lots

explanation.surface: A seaman takes a gamble to back up his superior.
explanation.definitionFit: Matelot is British slang for a seaman.

clue.text: Record it's black inside a chimney

indicators.note: the colour letter goes inside the chimney word

parts.note: lum is a Scottish and northern word for chimney
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A recording turns out to be sooty inside a chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a long-playing record.

clue.text: Uneven acquisition representative secured

indicators.note: the purchase word holds the politician fast inside

parts.note: a buy is a purchase
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An uneven deal was obtained by an agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumpy surface is rough and irregular.

clue.text: Am afraid to invest minimum amount — try first for sponsor

indicators.note: the try word is placed at the front of the answer

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt

indicators.note: to invest is to surround or besiege, so the coin goes inside

parts.note: daren't means am afraid to
P, a penny, is the smallest coin

explanation.surface: Fearful of investing even a little, someone first seeks a backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest' sounds financial but means to surround.
explanation.definitionFit: A godparent sponsors a child at baptism.

clue.text: Poor images of musical redesigned by artist

indicators.note: redesign suggests the letters are reworked into a fresh order

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: Weak portraits from a show reworked by a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Simulacra are representations, often unsatisfactory imitations.

clue.text: Benefit from a curtain-call?

indicators.note: a call is something spoken, so the curtain word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a veil is a hanging curtain of fabric

explanation.surface: An actor gains from taking a bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtain-call' suggests a theatre bow, but splits into a curtain and a call.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail as a noun means use or benefit, as in to no avail.

clue.text: Plaything that's timeless, repeatedly coming back

definitions.text: Plaything that's timeless, repeatedly coming back

indicators.note: the piece is said again, so it appears twice
returning means the shortened word is read backwards
without time removes the time abbreviation from the word

parts.note: a toy is a plaything

explanation.surface: A toy that never ages keeps returning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' drops T from TOY to leave OY; 'coming back' turns it to YO; 'repeatedly' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: This spinning toy on a string keeps returning to the hand.

clue.text: Friendly sign-off from elite group

definitions.meaning: a warm closing for a letter, wishing someone well
the finest people, the cream of the crop

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a closing goodwill wish; the other is the very finest of all.
